newsitem.title: USA: Most NYMEX natgas ends up, gains more on ACCESS.
newsitem.headline: Most NYMEX natgas ends up, gains more on ACCESS.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended up Tuesday in a moderate session, with a rocketing spot-December contract on forecasts for colder weather this week dragging most of the complex higher.

December surged 32.8 cents to close at $3.306 per million British thermal units, then rallied to another new high of $3.40 on ACCESS. Jan, which also hit a new high of $3.24 in after-hours trade, earlier settled 26.2 cents higher at $3.17.
"We went out on the highs and there has to be more to come. I wouldn't get in the way of it right now," said one East Coast trader, noting a lot of cold weather ahead.
And with storage operators likely to remain cautious about early-season withdrawals, most expected a buoyant physical market heading into bidweek later this week.
While technical traders said December was overbought and due for a pullback after a 25 percent rally in four sessions, they said anything could happen ahead of spot expiry Thursday.
"It seems way overdone, but we could go even higher," said another eastern trader.

Chartists pegged next December resistance at the spot continuation settlement of $3.448 from December 21 and then at the all-time intraday high of $3.72 set the same date. Support was seen at $3.10, then at $2.88 and then in the mid-$2.70s.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices jumped more than 10 cents Tuesday to about the $3.00 level. Midwest pipes climbed 10-15 cents to the low-to-mid $2.80s. New York city gate swing gas gained 10 cents or more to the $3.60s. December gas in New York was still quoted at about $1.35 over the NYMEX screen.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip gained 8.8 cents to $2.399. NYMEX said 73,866 Hub contracts traded, up sharply from Monday's revised tally of 48,795.
NYMEX December Alberta natgas closed 13.5 cents higher at $1.75. Deferred contracts were untraded. NYMEX said four Alberta contracts traded versus 122 on Monday.
NYMEX December Permian natgas ended 22 cents higher at $2.95, while deferreds were untraded. NYMEX said 30 Permian lots changed hands after eight consecutive days of no activity.

On the KCBT, December finished 28 cents higher at $3.05, while forward months settled up by 1.5 to 10 cents. The East/West spread widened by 4.8 cents to 25.6 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 851 contracts traded, up from Monday's volume of 331.
KCBT December natgas expires Friday, November 22.
